1Purpose

This policy is the frame for the module at [Provider name]. It names the seven standards we work to and the policy that carries each one, the roles that run the module, and the rules that apply across the whole module. It sets no time limit and restates no commitment of its own: each of POL-ECS-02 to POL-ECS-08 holds its commitments, its clocks and its checks in one place. It is for families, our workers, the other services in a 's team, and the people who check our work.

2Applies to

  • Every child who receives early childhood supports from us, and their , from first contact until supports end.
  • Everyone who works for [Provider name] and has contact with those children or families: employees, contractors, students, volunteers and key personnel.
  • Every place we work: the family home, early learning and school settings, community places, our premises, and phone or video sessions.
  • A sole trader or partnership registered for these supports, in the same way as a larger provider.

This policy is the shared frame for the module. POL-ECS-02 to POL-ECS-08 each set out one standard in full, with its own commitments, times and checks; nothing in this policy changes them. POL-CHS-01 Child Safe Policy sets the child safety rules for all our work with children; until it is written, the appendix to POL-ECS-02 holds the state and territory reporting schedule.

3Commitments

C1

We will do what POL-ECS-02 The Child Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (the child, s 56).

C2

We will do what POL-ECS-03 The Family Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (the family, s 57).

C3

We will do what POL-ECS-04 Inclusion Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (inclusion, s 58).

C4

We will do what POL-ECS-05 Collaboration Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (collaboration, s 59).

C5

We will do what POL-ECS-06 Capacity Building Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (capacity building, s 60).

C6

We will do what POL-ECS-07 Evidence-Informed Practice Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (evidence-informed supports, s 61).

C7

We will do what POL-ECS-08 Outcome Based Approach Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (outcome based approach, s 62).

4Ground rules

G1

A child's safety comes before everything else in this policy. A worker who is worried about a child acts on that worry first.

G2

A person with decides about the child's supports. We ask for the child's own views in a way that fits their age and how they communicate, and we record them.

G3

One route for every concern. A practice concern goes to the . A conduct or safety concern about a colleague or a manager goes to the Chief Executive. A concern about the Chief Executive or an owner goes to the chair of the governing body, or in a sole trader's business to the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register. A child who may be at goes to the the same day, under PRO-ECS-02 The Child Procedure (Early Childhood Supports). The person a concern is about never handles it.

G4

The time limits of the module are set in POL-ECS-02 to POL-ECS-08 and the procedures under them; the Module clocks table at the end of these ground rules reproduces them, and this policy sets none of its own. Where the law sets a shorter time, the shorter time applies.

G5

The appendix to POL-ECS-02 holds the state and territory reporting schedule: the law of [state or territory] on who must report, the test, where, how fast, and the duty of every adult to tell police of child sexual abuse. POL-CHS-01, when written, holds the wider child safe standards and reportable conduct rules. The Quality Manager checks the schedule every 12 months and when the law changes.

G6

Each fact is held once. REG-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Register is the one register for the module and holds dates, names, counts and record numbers. The forms hold the detail and the family's words.

G7

A family can say no to a , a referral, a team meeting or a question. Saying no is recorded and is never a reason to reduce supports.

G8

A complaint made by a child or family at any point is handled under PRO-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Procedure. A child's "stop" or "not happy" signal is a complaint the child can make in their own way.

G9

A sole trader holds every role except practice supervisor and . An outside practice supervisor with early childhood experience and the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register are the checks on the sole trader's own work.

G10

The is the practitioner accountable for the child's plan and the register row. Where the family chooses a key worker from our team, the key worker is the plan lead, and when the key worker changes the plan-lead role moves with it the same day.

9Words we use

345 words
early childhood supports
supports for a young child with developmental delay or disability, and their family, under the registration class "early intervention supports for early childhood".
family
the parents, carers and other people who raise the child, as the family itself describes them.
parental responsibility
the legal authority to make decisions for a child. A court or child protection order can change who holds it.
support network
the relatives, friends, educators and others in the child's everyday life whom the family chooses to involve.
everyday routines
the things the child does most days, such as meals, play, bath time, getting dressed and going to early learning.
key worker
the one practitioner the family chooses as their main contact. Where the family chooses a key worker, that person is the plan lead.
team around the child
the family, our practitioners and the other providers who work together on the child's plan.
plan lead
the practitioner accountable for the child's plan and the register row.
practice supervisor
the clinical supervisor of the early childhood practitioners.
practitioner drafting for the plan lead
the practitioner the plan lead asks to draft the plan under PRO-ECS-08. The plan lead stays accountable for the plan.
functional outcome
something the child will do in daily life, written so the family can see when it has happened.
coaching
helping a parent, carer or educator practise a strategy in their own routine, in place of doing it for them.
both clearances
an NDIS worker screening clearance, and the working with children check of [state or territory].
child safety lead
the role the Chief Executive names to receive every concern about a child and to see that reports are made.
risk of harm
the words this module uses for the reporting threshold. Our test is that you suspect on reasonable grounds that a child is at risk of harm. The appendix to POL-ECS-02 gives the exact term used in [state or territory].
business day
a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.

1Purpose

This policy sets what [Provider name] commits to for each who receives . The child knows and uses their rights, is safe, and keeps their supports when something has to change. It is for children, their families, our workers and the people who check our work.

2Applies to

  • Every child who receives early childhood supports from us, and their .
  • Everyone who works for [Provider name] and has contact with those children: employees, contractors, students, volunteers and key personnel.
  • Every place we support a child: their home, early learning and school settings, the community, our premises, our vehicles, and phone or video sessions.
  • A sole trader or partnership, in the same way as a larger provider.

This policy sits under POL-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Policy. POL-CHS-01 Child Safe Policy sets the child safe rules for all our work with children. Until POL-CHS-01 is written, the appendix to this policy holds the state and territory reporting schedule; that appendix is the schedule POL-CHS-01 will hold, and it has one owner, the Quality Manager. Where either sets a shorter time or a stricter rule, that one applies.

3Commitments

C1

We will tell each child and their family what the child's rights are and how to raise a concern. We use the way the child communicates. We agree with the child how they show "stop" or "not happy", and we give them a child-sized way to complain: a picture card, or a trusted adult they name. A "stop" or "not happy" signal repeated across two sessions is logged and reviewed with the family. We do this by the end of the first session and at every plan review, and we record what we covered.

We tell police, the reportable conduct scheme and the screening unit as the law of [state or territory] requires. 4Ground rules

G1

A child's safety comes before rosters, paperwork and our reputation.

G2

Every child has the rights below, and every procedure under this policy respects them. The child has the right to be safe, to be heard, and to be told what is happening in a way they understand. The child has the right to respect and dignity, and to have their body and privacy respected. The child has the right to have their family, culture and language respected. The child has the right to play, learn and take part. The child has the right to say stop and have a worker listen. The child has the right to complain, with help. The child has the right to be treated no worse because of their disability.

G3

No worker needs a manager's permission to call 000 or to report to the child protection authority. A legal duty to report can belong to the worker personally. Telling the child safety lead does not remove it. In [state or territory] every adult must tell police of a reasonable belief that a child has been sexually abused (statutory in Victoria, New South Wales, Queensland and the ACT). Telling the child safety lead or the child protection authority does not discharge that duty either.

G4

You do not need proof. A reasonable suspicion is enough: report when you suspect on reasonable grounds that a child is at risk of harm. Nobody waits for proof, and nobody investigates before reporting.

G5

A report to the child protection authority needs no consent from the child or the family.

G6

Workers never question a child to get detail, never promise to keep a secret, and never tell the person a concern is about.

G7

The person a concern is about never receives, manages or closes it. A concern about a worker goes to the child safety lead. A concern about the lead goes to the deputy. A concern about a manager goes to the child safety lead and the Chief Executive. A concern about the Chief Executive or an owner goes to the chair of the governing body. In a sole trader's business it goes to the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register.

G8

Moving a worker away from children while a concern is looked into is a safety step. It is not a finding.

G9

The law of [state or territory] decides who must report, on what ground, to whom and how fast. The appendix to this policy holds the state and territory reporting schedule; it is the schedule POL-CHS-01 will hold when it is written, and it has one owner, the Quality Manager. It is completed at adoption, and the Quality Manager checks it every 12 months and when the law changes. POL-CHS-01 holds the wider child safe rules.

G10

Nobody is punished or disadvantaged for raising a concern about a child in good faith. The NDIS Act 2013 also protects a person who tells the NDIS Commission or our key personnel about a suspected breach of the Act.

G11

When a child's wishes and the family's wishes differ, we record both. A safety decision never waits for agreement.

G12

FRM-ECS-01 is restricted to the child safety lead, the deputy and the Chief Executive. The Quality Manager and auditors read REG-INC-01 and REG-ECS-01 col J, not the form. The receives only the outcome for the child's supports and plan (FRM-ECS-01 Q14 and Q18), by note. The REG-INC-01 row for a concern is restricted to those three and the authorised notifier. REG-ECS-01 col J holds record numbers only.

G13

Each fact is held once. FRM-ECS-01 holds the child protection detail. Where the concern is connected with our supports or one of our workers, it is also an incident: FRM-INC-01 holds the worker's account and REG-INC-01 holds the row. Where it is not, FRM-ECS-01 Section A holds the worker's account and there is no incident row. REG-ECS-01 holds the dates and record numbers.

1Purpose

The result: each 's rights are explained and used every day. Each type of setting has a safety assessment, and each child has agreed controls, before a practitioner sees the child. A worry about a child's safety is reported on the day. When a session or practitioner changes, the child's supports carry on the way the agreed.

This procedure gives effect to POL-ECS-02 The Child Policy (Early Childhood Supports). Steps 1 and 2 give effect to C2, C4, C5 and C6. Steps 3 and 4 give effect to C1 and C3. Step 5 gives effect to C12. Step 6 gives effect to C13. Steps 7 to 9 give effect to C2 and C6. Steps 10 to 25 give effect to C7 to C11. Steps 26 to 30 give effect to C14.

"The " means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Incident Management and Reportable Incidents) Rules 2018. Every concern about a child has a record in FRM-ECS-01. A concern is also an incident only where the harm is connected with the provision of our supports or with one of our workers (the Incident Rules, sections 9, 15(2) and 20(1)); it then also has one incident report (FRM-INC-01) and one row in REG-INC-01 Incident Register. A concern about harm at home or elsewhere that is not connected with our supports is a child protection report, not an NDIS incident: FRM-ECS-01 Section A holds the practitioner's account and no NDIS Commission notice is made. Decision table 2 makes the split.

2When and who

Start at the point that matches:

  • Before a worker's first contact with a child, and before the first session in any setting: steps 1 and 2.
  • At the first session and at every plan review: steps 3 to 6.
  • In every session: steps 7 to 9.
  • When anyone is worried that a child is at : steps 10 to 25.
  • When a session or practitioner has to change: steps 26 to 30.

Who acts:

  • The practitioner at the session, for every session and every concern.
  • The , for the first session, plan reviews and changes.
  • The Service Manager, for checks, observation, the setting-type safety assessments and unplanned changes.
  • The , for every concern after the worker's call. The acts when the lead is away or is the subject.
  • The Quality Manager, as authorised notifier for the NDIS Commission.
  • The Chief Executive, when a concern is about one of our workers, managers or owners.

A sole trader is the plan lead, the child safety lead and the worker. They name a deputy and an in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register. The independent contact receives any concern about the sole trader. The sole trader checks their own clearances and training at step 1. An outside observes the sole trader's sessions at step 9.

3Before you start

  • The child's row is open in REG-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Register.
  • You have the phone numbers of the child safety lead, the deputy and the on-call manager.
  • You have the number of the child protection reporting line of [state or territory], from the POL-ECS-02 appendix.
  • You have a paper copy of FRM-ECS-01 and of FRM-INC-01 Incident Report Form in your kit.
  • At the first session you have STA-CHS-01 Child Safety: Plain Summary and STA-RGT-03 Participant Rights: Plain Summary.

4Watch out

  • A duty to report can be yours alone. The law of [state or territory] can make you personally responsible. Waiting for a manager can leave a child at risk and put you in breach of the law.
  • Questions can weaken a child's account. A leading question can damage what the child later tells police or child protection.
  • A promise of secrecy cannot be kept. You will have to tell someone to keep the child safe. The child then loses trust in you.
  • Telling the wrong person can put the child at risk. Telling the person a concern is about can lead to more harm. It can also lose evidence.
  • The NDIS Commission notice and the child protection report are two separate duties. One does not replace the other. The Commission's 24 hour clock runs from the first time any manager knows, day or night (our standard; the Rules say from when the provider becomes aware).
  • A photograph of a child's body can add to their distress and harm the case. Keep evidence as it is, unless police or child protection direct otherwise.

5Steps

Before the first session

Step 1

The Service Manager

Check that each worker named for the child is cleared, has signed the code of conduct and is trained.

Check three things in REG-HRM-01 Worker Screening Register and REG-HRM-02 Training and Competency Register. First, are verified and in date. Second, FRM-CHS-01 Child Safe Code of Conduct and Acknowledgement is signed. Third, child safety induction and children's rights training are done. PRO-HRM-03 Training and Competency Procedure sets the content. It covers a child's rights, signs of harm and grooming, and how to respond when a child tells you something. It also covers the reporting duties of [state or territory] and cultural safety for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children. Give the worker the numbers of the child safety lead, the deputy and the on-call manager. Repeat all of this for a replacement worker. If a clearance is suspended, barred or refused, end the worker's contact with children that day and tell the Chief Executive.

Result
Only a cleared, signed and trained worker has contact with the child.
Record
REG-ECS-01 col AB
Time limit
Before the worker's first contact with the child. Again on each clearance expiry date, and the same day we learn a clearance is suspended, barred or refused (our standard)

Step 2

The plan lead

Agree this child's safety controls with the family, against the assessment for each type of setting.

A FRM-CHS-02 Child Safety Risk Assessment is held for each type of setting we work in: a family home, an early learning service or school, a community place, and phone or video. The Service Manager keeps them in REG-RSK-01 Risk Register and reviews them every 12 months. For this child, read the assessment for each setting type the child will be seen in, then agree a short controls line with the family (FRM-CHS-02 Part B, two or three lines): one to one support, personal care, transport, online contact, photographs and who else will be there. Write the controls line and the REG-RSK-01 number in REG-ECS-01 col I. Redo the controls line when the controls this child needs change: a new type of setting, a change in the child's needs, or a concern. Tell each worker of a new control before their next session.

Each setting type has a current assessment, and this child's controls are agreed and on file.

First session and each plan review

Step 3

The plan lead

Explain the child's rights and how to raise a concern to the child and the family.

Use the way the child communicates: words, pictures, key word sign or an interpreter. Give the family STA-CHS-01 and STA-RGT-03. Cover the rights in POL-ECS-02 G2, what adults may and may not do under the code of conduct, and who to tell. Book an interpreter if the family wants one. Show the family how they can complain, under PRO-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Procedure. Give the child their own way: agree with the child how they will show "stop" or "I am not happy", and a picture card or a trusted adult they name that they can use to complain. Write it in the communication section of FRM-ECS-07 Child and Family Support Plan. A "stop" or "not happy" signal repeated across two sessions is logged on FRM-ECS-05 and reviewed with the family. If the child cannot take part, use pictures or a familiar object with a parent present. Try again at the next session.

The child and the family know the child's rights, and the child has a way to say they are unsafe or unhappy.

Step 4

The plan lead

Ask the child for their own views.

Ask in the child's way and at their pace. Ask what they like, what they do not like and what they want from sessions. If the child does not use words, watch and note what they show. Write what the child said or showed, then what we did about it. If the family wants something different, record both.

The child's own views are on record and shape what we do.

7If it goes wrong

  • You cannot reach the child safety lead or the deputy. Phone the on-call manager, then the Chief Executive. Do not wait to report: if you suspect on reasonable grounds that the child is at risk of harm, report yourself (step 14).
  • The lead decides not to report and you suspect on reasonable grounds that the child is at risk of harm. Report yourself (step 14). You do not need permission. Tell the Chief Executive afterwards. You may also tell the NDIS Commission.
  • The authority's line is busy, or gives no reference number. Try the online report if there is one. If the child is in danger, call 000. Write each time you tried and tell the child safety lead.
  • A report was late or was not made. The child safety lead makes it now, tells the Chief Executive the same day, and writes the reason at FRM-ECS-01 Q17. The Quality Manager adds the cause to REG-QMS-01 Continuous Improvement Register.
  • A notice will miss its time limit. The authorised notifier tells the Chief Executive before the limit passes, gives the notice as soon as possible, and records the reason.
  • The concern is about the lead, a manager, the Chief Executive or the sole trader. Use Decision table 1. You may also report to the child protection authority and to the NDIS Commission. POL-GOV-03 Whistleblower and Disclosure Protection Policy protects you.
  • A child says nothing, but you are worried by what you see. Do not press. Write what you saw, tell the lead the same day, and ask the lead to apply Decision table 2.
  • A family member, school or another provider tells us of a concern. Write down what they say, in their words, and tell the child safety lead the same day.
  • A setting-type assessment is missing or overdue, or this child's controls line is not on file. For a new child, no session goes ahead until the controls line is agreed (step 2). For an overdue setting-type assessment, the Service Manager redoes it within 5 business days, and sessions continue under the controls already agreed.
  • The family refuses a control. The session does not go ahead in that setting until a control is agreed. Offer another setting and tell the Service Manager. If the refusal worries you, treat it as a concern (step 13).
  • A trained worker is absent. Do not send a worker who has not passed step 1. Use step 27.
  • A plan review is overdue. The plan lead repeats steps 3, 4 and 6 at the next contact and tells the Service Manager.
  • The plan lead is away for more than 5 business days. The Service Manager names another worker to take the steps, and tells the family.
  • The family says no to the support network, or to sharing information. Record it in their words. It is never a reason to reduce supports.

8Done means

For a new child:

  • Every worker named in REG-ECS-01 col AB is cleared, signed and trained.
  • Each setting type the child is seen in has a current assessment in REG-RSK-01, and this child's controls line is in REG-ECS-01 col I.
  • By the end of the first session, REG-ECS-01 col H shows the rights explained and REG-ECS-01 col Y shows the continuity arrangement. REG-ECS-01 col AH shows the child's views.
  • The child has a way to say they are unsafe or unhappy in their plan. REG-ECS-01 col E and col S show who the family involved.

For a concern about a child:

  • The child is safe, and a report is made or the reason it was not is recorded in FRM-ECS-01.
  • FRM-ECS-01 and the numbers in REG-ECS-01 col J exist. Where the concern is connected with our supports, FRM-INC-01 and a row in REG-INC-01 exist and are linked to it.
  • Every other notice is recorded in FRM-ECS-01 Q16 (and FRM-INC-01 Q28 where the concern is an incident), and the family was told or the reason is recorded.
  • The family was offered an advocate and interim safety actions are in place. The record is closed with every notice inside its time.

For a change:

  • REG-ECS-01 col Z shows the notice given, what replaced the session, whether it followed col Y, and the family's view.

9Quick card

147 words
  • Danger now, or a crime: call 000 (step 11).
  • Stay with the child and keep them safe (step 10).
  • Listen. Do not question. Do not promise secrecy. Write the exact words (step 12).
  • If you suspect on reasonable grounds that the child is at risk of harm: report to the child protection authority now (step 14). You need no permission.
  • Then phone the child safety lead straight after. In every other case, phone the lead as soon as the child is safe and the same day at the latest (step 13).
  • Write FRM-ECS-01 Section A the same day, and the incident report where the harm is connected with our supports (step 15).
  • Every session: follow the safety controls (step 8) and use the child's rights (step 7).
  • Before first contact: cleared, signed and trained (step 1).
  • When a session changes: follow what the family agreed (step 27).

form.intro:
Use this record for every concern that a child is at , from anyone, in any place. It shows why we suspect, on reasonable grounds, that the child is at risk. It shows the report made to the child protection authority of [state or territory], and what happened next.

  • Section A: the practitioner who has the concern completes this the same day.
  • Section B: the child safety lead completes this during the worker's first call.
  • Section C: the person who made the report to the authority completes this. That is the worker, or the child safety lead.
  • Sections D and E: the child safety lead completes these as the concern is managed.

This record sits beside the incident report only where the harm is connected with the provision of our supports or with one of our workers (PRO-ECS-02 Decision table 2). In that case the worker's account of what happened goes on FRM-INC-01 Incident Report Form, as for any incident, and question 4 here is a short reason only. Where the concern is not connected with our supports, there is no incident report and no NDIS Commission notice: question 4 carries the full account.

Phone the child safety lead before you start writing. If a child is in danger, call 000 first.

Have ready: the child's name, date of birth and address, and the names of the people who live with them. Have the reference number the authority gave you.

What happens next: the child safety lead gives this record a number and enters it in REG-ECS-01 col J. PRO-ECS-02 The Child Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) sets every step. When systems are down, use the paper copy kept at [location at each site].
form.privacy:
We collect this information to keep a child safe and to make reports under child protection law. We also collect it to meet our duties under the NDIS Act 2013.

Only the child safety lead, the and the Chief Executive read it. The Quality Manager and auditors read REG-INC-01 and REG-ECS-01 col J, not this form. The and the Service Manager receive only the outcome for the child's supports and plan (questions 14 and 18), by note. We give parts of it to the child protection authority, police, the NDIS Commission and other bodies. We do this when the law requires or allows it. A report to the authority needs no consent.

A person with parental responsibility can ask what we hold about their child. We may hold back parts if giving them could put the child at risk. We also hold back parts if the law or an authority tells us not to. We remove other people's details first. We never tell the person a concern is about who raised it. POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets how we store and protect this record.
form.after:
• Practitioner: phone the child safety lead first. Give Section A to the child safety lead, and to nobody else, the same day (our standard).
  • If the concern is about the child safety lead, give it to the deputy. If it is about the deputy, give it to the lead. If it is about a manager, give it to the lead and the Chief Executive. If it is about the Chief Executive or an owner, give it to the chair of the governing body. In a sole trader's business, give it to the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register.
  • You can also report straight to the child protection authority or the NDIS Commission. POL-GOV-03 Whistleblower and Disclosure Protection Policy sets out how you are protected.
  • Child safety lead: complete Section B within 1 hour of the worker's call (our standard).
  • Child safety lead: give the record its number and enter it in REG-ECS-01 col J the same day (our standard).
  • Child safety lead: complete Section D within 1 of the concern (our standard).
  • Child safety lead: add dated entries to Section E until the record is closed. Read every open record at least every 20 business days (our standard).
  • Keep the closed record in the restricted section of the child's file. Keep it for 45 years from the day it is made (Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, recommendation 8.1; check the records law of [state or territory] at adoption). Where the concern is also an incident, the , section 12(4), minimum of 7 years applies as well. REG-ECS-01 sets the same period for the row where col J holds this record's number.

register.proves:
This register holds one row for every who receives from [Provider name]. The row is the index to the child's file. It shows who the is, who is in the team, what the family agreed to, and when each plan, review and report was due and done.

  • Indicators evidenced: s 56 (1) to s 56 (4), s 56 (5)(a) and s 56 (5)(b).
  • Also s 57 (1) to s 57 (8), on the family.
  • Also s 58 (1) to s 58 (4), on inclusion, and s 59 (1) to s 59 (4), on collaboration.
  • Also s 60 (1) to s 60 (5), on capacity building, and s 61 (2), on practitioner skills.
  • Also s 62 (1) to s 62 (6), on outcomes.
  • Legal basis: National Disability Insurance Scheme (Provider Registration and Practice Standards) Rules 2018, Schedule 5, clauses 3 to 9. Section 20(3), item 18 of those Rules applies Schedules 1 and 5 to early intervention supports for early childhood.
  • No NDIS instrument sets the columns of this register. The columns are our standard, built from the indicators.
  • Each fact is held once. The forms hold the detail and the family's words. This register holds the dates, the names, the counts, the record numbers and a one-line pointer to the form.
  • Clearances and training are in REG-HRM-01 Worker Screening Register and REG-HRM-02 Training and Competency Register. Intake and the service agreement are in REG-SUP-01 Participant and Service Agreement Register (Rise version not yet written); until it exists, column F holds who has .
  • Retention: keep each row for 7 years after supports end, or until the child turns 25, whichever is later (our standard; NDIS Act 2013, section 45B (from 27 August 2026): records of claims and supports are kept for 7 years).
  • Retention where column J holds a record number: keep the row for 45 years (Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, recommendation 8.1; our standard). Check the child safe and records law of [state or territory] at adoption and before any row is destroyed.

Columns A to G and I are filled before the first session, and columns H and Y by the end of it. Column J stays blank until a record exists. Columns K to X and AH are filled as the plan is made and followed. Columns Z, AA and AD are filled when an , a transition or an exit comes up. Columns AB, AC, AE, AF, AG, AI, AJ, AK and AL are kept current for every row.
register.entry:
1. The opens the row within 2 of the family accepting our offer (our standard). The Service Manager names the plan lead that day.
  2. Use one row for each child. Brothers and sisters each get their own row, linked in column AF.
  3. Fill columns A to G and I before the first session. Column J stays blank until a record exists. The first session does not go ahead while column I is empty for the type of setting it is in.
  4. Fill columns H and Y by the end of the first session.
  5. Fill every other column within 2 business days of the form or meeting that produces it (our standard).
  6. Write "not yet asked" with a date when a required answer is not known. Ask at the next contact with the family.
  7. Never overwrite or delete an entry. A correction is a new version of the row, with the date, your name and the reason.
  8. Columns H, N, R, X, Z, AH, AI, AJ and AK hold dated entries. Add each new entry underneath the last one. Column AL holds one date, replaced at each check.
  9. The family's own words stay in the forms (FRM-ECS-02, FRM-ECS-03, FRM-ECS-05). This register holds dates, names, counts, record numbers and one-line pointers. Where a short phrase of the family's is entered, such as "none wanted" in column N, it is entered as it was said, signed or shown. Nobody tidies it.
  10. Column J takes record numbers only. Never write what was seen, said or suspected in this register.
  11. When the plan lead is away for more than 5 business days, the Service Manager names another worker to keep the row.
  12. When the system is down, complete the paper forms. Enter the row within 1 business day of the system coming back.
  13. A sole trader is the plan lead and keeps every row.

A row is closed only when all of these are true:

  • column AD is filled and column AC says "exited"
  • the family has their final progress report and their copy of the last plan
  • column AA shows the handover was given, or the family's decision that none was wanted
  • every consent line in column Q has a withdrawn date or an end date
  • nothing in column AE, AI, AJ, AK or AL is still due.
